ready1_open_rewrite.title: Dataset open-ended question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Four vials were set up to investigate bacterial transformation. Vials 1 and 2 each contained E. coli bacteria that had been made competent and had then been mixed with a plasmid containing the gene for ampicillin (pAMP) resistance. Vials 3 and 4 both contained E. coli that had also been made competent but had not been mixed with a plasmid. Each vial of bacteria was poured onto a nutrient agar plate. Vials 1 and 3 were poured onto plates that contained the antibiotic ampicillin. Vials 2 and 4 were poured onto plates that did not contain ampicillin. Explain why there was no growth on Plate 3.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are four nutrient agar plates in the image, respectively labeled as coming from test tubes/vials 1, 2, 3, 4. Plate 3 is labeled “From test tube 3”, and the inside of the plate is blank/clear, with no visible colony growth. Reasoning: The question stem states that although the E. coli in vial 3 were made competent, they were not mixed with the pAMP plasmid containing the ampicillin resistance gene; at the same time, vial 3 was poured onto a plate containing ampicillin. Bacteria that did not obtain the pAMP plasmid do not have ampicillin resistance, so they will be inhibited or killed by ampicillin and cannot grow. Therefore, Plate 3 has no growth because these bacteria were not transformed.
